title: How the build's sessions are organized: a coordinator per repo
why: Orchestrator, Oct 28 14:58 CDT: you proposed three tiers (coordinator, lane leads, triage, all Opus); an Opus blind review with web research says the shape is sound but the cut is wrong.
note: Home for the rulings: docs/decisions/session-tiers.md on main. One coordinator per repo; triage and a batch runner as standing sessions, started together by the coordinator before any lane, rotated before they go stale and archived only after draining; a session pushes back in one line when work reaches the wrong tier; shape is picked from the request (solo, one lane, coordinator). Rulings (shiv): item 50 b, lane sessions run Opus (Oct 28 16:15 CDT); item 53 a, a per-environment context window for cloud lanes, measured working Oct 28 17:53 CDT (lane read max_tokens 200000); item 59 a, keep today's helper-agent model table until a lane measures cost and quality (Oct 28 17:50 CDT); item 67 a, Opus grants live on the roadmap step (Oct 29 13:44 CDT; step opus-grant-on-step). Grant: "have just opus review building this out" (Oct 28 15:04 CDT). Built: L2 skills (#794, batch 17, main 134b23ca); L1 rules and glossary (#797, batch 18, main 1cc47f01); L3 session-start line (#800, batch 19 #801, main 0f6a1487, Oct 29 15:17 CDT). The batch runner runs since Oct 29 15:17 CDT (session_013NEJL1EEFHP9xvwiLRqMFt) and owns batches from batch 20 on. Left: item 59 a's measurement of helper-agent cost and quality. It has no brief or metric yet, so it is not ready. Placed after c200 (triage 12, Oct 28). Arbiter (item 81 a, Oct 29 16:42 CDT): started only when shiv tells the coordinator "spawn arbiter", for long runs; high effort by default; its answers rule in its repo below his. In #808.
